name: Cold compress / chilled washcloth
summary: A chilled cloth or pack held on the eyes to reduce morning puffiness; cold therapy has broader evidence, but not for eyes specifically.
lead: A cold compress or chilled washcloth is a home practice of holding a cold, damp cloth, gel pack or similar item against the closed eyes to reduce puffiness, often after waking.

name: Lymphatic drainage eye massage
summary: Light fingertip strokes around the eyes meant to move fluid and reduce puffiness; adapted from manual lymphatic drainage, which has mixed evidence even in lymphedema.
lead: Lymphatic drainage eye massage is a practice of gentle, light-pressure strokes around the eyes and face intended to move fluid and reduce puffiness. It is adapted from manual lymphatic drainage (MLD).

name: Eye yoga / eye exercises
summary: Eye movement and relaxation routines claimed to firm the eye area; no studies support an appearance effect.
lead: Eye yoga, or eye exercises, refers to routines of deliberate eye movements, palming, focus shifting and relaxation that practitioners say can relieve strain, improve vision and, in looksmaxxing circles, firm or brighten the skin around the eyes. The practice draws on a lineage that includes the Bates method, an alternative therapy developed by the American eye doctor William Horatio Bates (1860-1931).

name: Lemon / tomato juice for dark circles
summary: A DIY acid lightener for under-eye circles; untested, and citrus plus sun can cause lasting dark marks.
lead: Applying lemon juice or tomato juice under the eyes is a do-it-yourself remedy that online communities say lightens periorbital dark circles. Lemon is acidic and rich in vitamin C, while tomato juice contains lycopene and vitamin C, and proponents credit these for a "lightening" effect.

name: Screen time / blue light reduction
summary: Cutting screen time or blue light to ease eye strain; trials of blue-blockers are mostly negative and appearance effects are untested.
lead: Reducing screen time or blue light exposure, through breaks, filter glasses or night modes, is discussed in looksmaxxing circles as a way to ease eye strain and the tired look around the eyes. Computer vision syndrome describes eye strain, dryness, headache and blurred vision after prolonged screen use.

name: Hypoallergenic bedding / dust mite control
summary: Allergen-proof bedding to limit mites; useful for dust allergy, untested for facial puffiness.
lead: Hypoallergenic bedding and dust mite control means using allergen-proof covers, hot washing and humidity reduction to limit mite allergens, which looksmaxxing communities sometimes link to morning facial puffiness or allergic-looking eyes. House dust mites live in bedding and feed on shed skin, and are a common cause of allergic rhinitis and asthma.

name: Creatine water retention concerns
summary: Whether creatine puffs the face; water goes into muscle per reviews, facial effects untested.
lead: Creatine water retention concerns refers to worries in looksmaxxing communities that creatine supplements cause facial bloating or puffiness. Reference sources describe early weight gain from creatine as water moving into muscle, mainly during loading.

name: Elevated head sleeping / wedge pillow
summary: Raising the head while asleep to cut morning puffiness; proven for reflux, untested for looks.
lead: Sleeping with the head raised, using a wedge pillow or bed risers, is said by looksmaxxing communities to reduce morning facial puffiness from fluid pooling. Head-of-bed elevation is an established lifestyle measure for reflux.

name: Lymphatic drainage massage
summary: Light-pressure facial and body massage meant to move fluid along lymph pathways; popular for 'debloating' the face, with clinical research limited to lymphedema.
lead: Lymphatic drainage massage, usually called manual lymphatic drainage (MLD), is a form of gentle skin manipulation based on the hypothesis that it encourages lymph to move away from tissues toward the heart. Practitioners use light pressure and slow, rhythmic circular movements rather than the deeper pressure of conventional massage.
claims: Facial puffiness is often lymphatic fluid, not fat or bone structure
Daily facial massage routines (up to three times a day) improve facial definition
Cardio such as jump rope aids lymphatic drainage
Nasal breathing and tongue posture indirectly improve lymph flow in the face

name: Face yoga / face exercises
summary: Repeated facial-muscle movements promoted for toning and de-puffing the face; small studies exist but good evidence for appearance changes is limited.
lead: Face yoga, also called face exercises, is a set of routines involving repeated contraction, stretching or massage of facial muscles. It is promoted as a non-surgical way to look younger, tone the face and reduce puffiness.

name: Low-sodium diet
summary: Restricting dietary sodium, a medical strategy for blood pressure, also used in looksmaxxing circles to reduce water retention and facial puffiness.
lead: A low-sodium diet is an eating pattern that limits sodium intake, typically to between 1,500 and 2,300 mg per day. It is used in managing hypertension, heart failure and kidney disease, and it emphasizes fresh, unprocessed foods over packaged ones.

name: Gluten-free diet for bloat
summary: Dropping gluten to cut bloating and facial puffiness; medically indicated for celiac disease, with no evidence found for face-puff use in people without gluten-related conditions.
lead: A gluten-free diet excludes gluten, the group of proteins in wheat, barley, rye and related grains. Lifelong adherence is the only medically accepted treatment for celiac disease.

name: Water cutting / dehydration
summary: Deliberate fluid loss to look leaner or make weight; documented in combat sports, with dehydration-related deaths and regulator responses.
lead: Water cutting is the practice of rapidly reducing body water, usually to make a lower weight class in combat sports or rowing, and in some communities to appear leaner. Methods include restricting food and fluids, water-loading, sweating through exercise, sweatsuits and saunas.

name: Cardio / sweating
summary: Exercising to sweat out fluid for a leaner, less puffy look; sweat is mostly water, so the physiology is known but appearance effects are untested here.
lead: Sweating is the release of fluid by sweat glands, which in humans mainly regulates temperature. Heat and muscle exertion increase output, and sweat is mostly water with small amounts of sodium, potassium and other solutes.

name: Sauna / steam
summary: Heat and steam sessions folded into skincare and wellness routines; the research is about the heart, not the face.
lead: A sauna is a heated room or bathhouse used for sweating, and the word comes from Finnish. Steam rooms, such as the hammam, are a related practice that runs cooler and at close to full humidity . In looksmaxxing communities, sauna and steam sessions are discussed as a lifestyle habit for "sweating", skin and general wellbeing.

name: Coffee / green tea ritual
summary: Caffeine drinks used as a de-puffing routine; no study has tested the face effect.
lead: The coffee or green tea ritual refers to drinking caffeinated beverages as part of a routine aimed at reducing facial puffiness or improving appearance. Both beverages contain caffeine, and green tea also contains polyphenols such as EGCG .

name: Thyroid/hypothyroid evaluation
summary: Checking thyroid function as a medical explanation for a puffy face; clinical, not cosmetic.
lead: Thyroid evaluation means testing for hypothyroidism, a condition in which the thyroid does not make enough hormone. In appearance discussions it is raised as a possible medical cause of a persistently puffy face .

name: Alcohol cutting (quit drinking)
summary: Quitting or cutting alcohol for less puff and better skin; the face effect itself is little studied.
lead: Alcohol cutting means reducing or stopping alcohol, which looksmaxxing communities discuss as a way to reduce facial puffiness and improve skin.

name: Facial icing with green tea ice cubes
summary: Rubbing frozen green tea on the face for de-puffing; untested for this use.
lead: Facial icing with green tea ice cubes is a social media skincare practice in which frozen brewed green tea is rubbed on the face, with proponents citing reduced puffiness and calmer skin.

name: Pulsed dye laser for stretch marks
summary: A vascular laser aimed at fresh red stretch marks; trials are small and results are not firmly established.
lead: Pulsed dye laser (PDL) treatment for stretch marks (striae distensae) is an in-office procedure in which a laser emitting light absorbed by blood vessels is applied to early, red or purple stretch marks (striae rubra). It is discussed in looksmaxxing and skin-focused communities as a way to reduce the redness of newly formed marks before they fade to white.

name: Excimer laser for stretch marks
summary: A UV laser aimed at repigmenting white stretch marks; the sources show only a tiny early-phase study.
lead: The 308 nm excimer laser is an ultraviolet light device that is used in dermatology for conditions such as vitiligo and psoriasis. It has also been studied for white (mature) stretch marks, striae alba, which are pale because the skin has lost pigment .

name: PRP for stretch marks
summary: Concentrated platelets from your own blood, tried on stretch marks mostly as an add-on in small trials.
lead: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) for stretch marks involves processing a person's own blood to concentrate platelets and applying or injecting the product into stretch marks (striae distensae), often with microneedling or lasers. Proponents say the growth factors in platelets encourage collagen remodelling.

name: Subcision / TCA CROSS
summary: A needle procedure that cuts the fibres tying rolling acne scars down; small studies and reviews support it as part of combined care.
lead: Subcision is a minor surgical procedure for depressed (atrophic) scars in which a needle is inserted beneath the skin and moved to cut the fibrous bands that hold a scar down. It was named and described in 1995 by Orentreich and Orentreich as subcutaneous incisionless surgery for depressed scars and wrinkles . TCA CROSS (chemical reconstruction of skin scars) is a separate scar procedure that uses trichloroacetic acid; it is grouped with subcision in community discussion of scar treatment, but the sources reviewed for this article do not describe it in detail.
claims: Subcision can lift tethered acne scars that lasers and microneedling do not
Subcision stimulates collagen at the site

name: Cortisone injections for keloids
summary: A clinic-administered steroid injection into keloids, a long-standing option now being compared with newer agents in small trials.
lead: Intralesional corticosteroid injection, commonly with triamcinolone acetonide, is a treatment in which a corticosteroid is injected directly into a keloid, a raised scar that grows beyond the original wound. Wikipedia reports that intralesional corticosteroids were introduced in the mid-1960s and are said to reduce fibroblast activity, inflammation and itching .

name: Keloid surgery + radiation
summary: Cutting out a keloid and radiating the wound bed, a clinical standard for severe cases with many add-on studies.
lead: Keloid excision with adjuvant radiation therapy is a combination in which a keloid is surgically removed and the wound is then treated with radiation to reduce regrowth. Wikipedia reports that excision alone has a recurrence rate of 70 to 100 percent, that recurrences can be larger, and that adding radiation, pressure therapy or laser sharply lowers recurrence; it adds that radiation is not recommended for children because of growth-abnormality risk .

name: Mederma / onion extract scar gel
summary: Over-the-counter onion extract scar gel with mixed, limited trial evidence.
lead: Mederma is an over-the-counter brand of topical scar products whose best-known product, Mederma Advanced Scar Gel, contains an extract of onion bulb (Allium cepa) together with other ingredients such as allantoin. It is marketed for improving the appearance of scars from surgery, injury, burns and acne.
claims: Onion extract gel fades and softens scars
It works on old acne and pockmark scars

name: Bio-Oil
summary: Popular scar and stretch mark oil with no product-specific evidence found here.
lead: Bio-Oil is a commercial skincare oil marketed for improving the appearance of scars, stretch marks and uneven skin tone. It is a branded cosmetic product, not a drug.

name: Cocoa butter / shea / coconut oil
summary: Folk stretch mark moisturizers; reviews found no evidence they prevent marks.
lead: Cocoa butter, shea butter and coconut oil are plant fats widely used in moisturizers, soaps and lotions, and are a traditional folk choice for trying to prevent stretch marks in pregnancy.
claims: Cocoa butter, shea or coconut oil prevents stretch marks

name: Folliculitis shower hygiene (post-gym shower)
summary: Showering after sweat to limit body acne; suggested in general references, untested in trials.
lead: Showering soon after sweating is a hygiene habit that some people adopt to reduce body acne ("bacne") and folliculitis.

name: Loose cotton clothing / washing sheets
summary: Loose cotton and clean bedding to cut friction acne; suggested generally, untested.
lead: Wearing loose, breathable clothing such as cotton and washing bedding regularly are habits adopted to reduce friction- and occlusion-related acne.
